runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Dylan Cunha, placed twice from two runs on good ground — the step to good-to-soft and 5f (shortest trip so far) is the key query, but De Sousa can offset jumping tactics; the pace duel with Perfect Strike is the central risk to its chance|

runners_data.name: Ivory Moon
runners_data.note: Won on soft ground last time and that form gives her the most relevant conditions profile in this field; George Boughey's yard is in good form (4/22 over 14 days), and though Billy Loughnane will look to travel prominently, she races more naturally from midfield than the deep hold-up tag suggests — her pace-adaptability is a strength here|

runners_data.name: Perfect Strike
runners_data.note: William Haggas's runner has run 7th and 5th on good ground over 6f, and 5f on soft represents a different proposition; Cieren Fallon will push for the lead from draw 4 but a further drop in trip on slower ground after two uninspiring efforts raises legitimate questions about improvement|

runners_data.name: Warriors Chant

runners_data.name: Sinova

runners_data.name: Igrok
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's runner drops back to 5f after finishing 10th and 7th on good ground over 6f; the longer break (74 days) and limited improvement in form are concerns, and good-to-soft may not be the unlock — Marco Ghiani gives tactical options from draw 6 but the raw form leaves him as a place at best|

runners_data.name: Rapid Deployment
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett sends out a horse who has run 5th and 7th on good ground over 6f, and 55 days off does not obviously sharpen the profile; Rhys Clutterbuck from draw 2 could find a decent tracking position, but there is no evidence yet of the finishing kick needed to win on softer ground|

races.paceDynamic: Valdoro and Perfect Strike are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the gates on this 5f Sandown sprint, creating a genuinely contested early gallop even on good-to-soft ground. With two horses fighting for the same piece of real estate from draws 3 and 4, the pace will be honest rather than suicidal, but the battle for supremacy burns energy early and leaves the race vulnerable to a horse travelling smoothly just off the tempo. The midfield trio of Ivory Moon, Igrok, and Rapid Deployment sit in the slipstream, but Ivory Moon's redistribution means the field holds more pace-committed types than true hold-up horses — Valdoro and Perfect Strike are most likely to actually secure the front positions, with Igrok and Rapid Deployment the most genuinely detached. On good-to-soft, where early speed burns faster and the final climb at Sandown tests stamina, this race shape most favours a prominent racer who can track the duel just off the pace and pounce once the front-runners begin to empty.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel Suits Tracker
scenarios.trigger: If Valdoro and Perfect Strike fight for the lead and a prominent tracker collects them in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off on good-to-soft ground, leaving a well-placed prominent mover to sweep past in the closing stages; the Sandown 5f rises late and punishes those who over-exert early

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner — most likely Valdoro — establishes a clear advantage and controls the tempo uncontested
scenarios.body: With Perfect Strike either missing the break or conceding the lead, Valdoro dictates a measured pace and simply outstays rivals up the climb; this shape suits a front-runner who can switch from race-mode to cruise-control once clear

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Warriors Chant or Sinova show natural pace or race-savviness that scrambles the expected dynamic
scenarios.body: An unknown quantity with a strong handler (Haggas stablemate quality from Hannon or Moore) could take advantage of a muddled pace battle between the two confirmed leaders; novice races on soft ground occasionally produce big-field-style surprises from unexposed types

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Past All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely fierce and good-to-soft ground slows the front-runners enough for trailing horses to reel them in late
scenarios.body: An unusually hot pace combined with testing ground could see Igrok or Rapid Deployment — both with experience over this course's demands — close with purpose; however, neither has shown the gears to win this way, and the midfield redistribution dilutes confidence in this shape

watchPoints.text: Ivory Moon's soft-ground form (1/1 on similar going) is the standout conditions tick in the field — if Boughey and Loughnane deploy her prominently early, she could be very hard to pass before the line

The pace duel between Valdoro and Perfect Strike is likely to be resolved by the first furlong — watch which one concedes, because whichever does so without fighting will be conserving energy for a renewed challenge late
Warriors Chant and Sinova are complete unknowns on debut and either could introduce a wild card if they show natural early pace and slot in front of the confirmed leaders

Igrok's 74-day absence combined with a 10th-place finish last time flags fitness and form concerns — watch in the market for any late support that might indicate stable confidence not visible in the form book

The going is officially good-to-soft despite being logged as soft in the race header — if the ground is riding on the faster side of that range, it marginally improves conditions for front-runners Valdoro and Perfect Strike relative to the pace-duel scenario

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win over this course and distance on Good ground; sim-going figures are thin but positive, and the 18-day freshener suits Stuart Williams' horses — the danger is that Always Perfect will contest every yard of the lead and the subsequent energy cost on softened turf.|
runners_data.comment: Merrimack won three starts back but has posted back-to-back fourths since, and our figures rank him eighth of ten in this field. He has run over today's trip and going, and 18 days since his last run suggests he is fit, but the weight of 138 lb adds little appeal at these odds.

runners_data.name: Lazzar
runners_data.note: Charlie Wallis yard is quiet at present (0/2 in 14 days), and sim-going form is limited; though a natural prominent racer by inclination, the density of rivals ahead of him means he is unlikely to secure that position and will be racing against his grain throughout.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lazzar does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and has shaped with some promise — a second four starts back offset by a sixth two starts back — but a rating of 75 and 128 lb from stall six leave him facing an uphill task from midfield ranking.

runners_data.name: Hint Of Humour
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa is a significant booking and Tony Carroll sends runners in good form (5/41 in 14 days); sits in the prominent group but a NEUTRAL draw and a recent run 14 days ago keep him competitive — finishing positions consistently in the frame without winning suggests a horse that needs everything right.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Hint Of Humour faces a stiff task from stall three carrying 131 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and placed four times in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Moe's Legacy
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and tends to race in midfield; Harris yard quiet (0/4 in 14 days) and the 7-day turnaround is tight, though the horse has form figures of 2 on good and soft-ish surfaces; best watched rather than relied upon.|
runners_data.comment: Moe's Legacy shaped with promise when second three starts back and steps up as a lively threat here, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour off a quick seven-day turnaround; the concern is that she has been winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Always Perfect
runners_data.note: Progressive three-year-old with two wins in last six starts and a strong flat-track frontrunner profile; hg=t (tongue tie) worn, trainer Fellowes at 1/18 in the 14-day window suggests modest stable form but the horse's own form line is the most compelling front-running argument in this race.|
runners_data.comment: Always Perfect won last time out and also took a race three starts back, which counts in her favour, but ranked ninth of ten on our figures she faces a stiff ask here, and 132 lb is no help either.

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams pair in same race creates an interesting tactical dynamic; three-year-old filly with a win at 5f on Good ground and consistent placed efforts — drawn 4 gives her a clean path to track the leaders, and she is the prominent type most likely to actually hold that position given her trainer's record (6/25 in 14 days).|

runners_data.name: On Edge
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old gelding with prominent/hold-up versatility and two recent wins at 5-6f on Good ground; the headgear flag (visor) is consistent, LR=28 days is manageable, and a sim-going placed effort adds credibility — age is the only structural concern at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and a winner three starts ago, On Edge brings solid recent form into this, and his experience over today's trip and going counts in his favour; however, that seventh last time out and 137 lb to carry are clear negatives to weigh up.

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection, albeit at low confidence; hold-up profile (hg=p, hood) suits a race that should see the front end get tapped out, and a 3rd at 5f on Soft ground last time out directly maps to today's conditions — the 13-day freshener and a 7lb claiming allowance from Toby Moore are the two swing factors.|
runners_data.comment: Havana Smile shaped with plenty of promise when third last time out, returning after just 13 days, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the main risk is whether he can reproduce that level from stall ten carrying 137 lb.

runners_data.name: Isle Of Lismore
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old carrying a visor, with placed efforts on Soft and Standard at 5f recently; Billy Loughnane is an elite booking that elevates the chance, but the horse's form at these going conditions (0W in sim-going) raises questions about whether it can convert.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out after winning two starts back, Isle Of Lismore arrives on a sharp 15-day turnaround in fine heart, and his experience over today's trip and going is a clear asset; carrying 134 lb from stall one, he looks the one to side with.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Hold-up profile with a placed effort at 5f on Soft last time (4th/6f SOF) that establishes soft-ground credentials; Hannon yard sends two runners from 52 runners recently (modest) and the five-pound claiming allowance from Cronin is modest mitigation — needs a strong pace to set up its late run, which this race shape should provide.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked top of the field on our ratings, Cayman Tai has run over today's trip and going and arrives fit on just 11 days' rest, yet to score in his last six starts and with a trainer running at only 4% over the past fortnight, that stable dip is the primary concern.

races.paceDynamic: Merrimack and Always Perfect are confirmed front-runners and will fight for early control from stalls 8 and 2 respectively, creating a genuinely contested pace across Sandown's flat 5f on Good To Soft ground. With four runners wanting prominent positions — Lazzar, Hint Of Humour, Adalida, and Isle Of Lismore all pressing for the same real estate — there will be significant early congestion two to three furlongs out, and at least one of those prominent types will be shuffled wider or outpaced than ideal. The soft-ish ground will amplify the cost of that early battle, sapping the leaders and leaving them vulnerable to horses who can travel sweetly in midfield and produce a sustained late run. This race shape most favours genuine hold-up or late-midfield horses who can bypass the early chaos, with Havana Smile and Cayman Tai the profiles to watch as the pace tests the front-runners' stamina reserves on softened turf. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically secure their preferred positions — Merrimack and Always Perfect are likeliest to actually lead, with Adalida best placed among the prominent brigade to hold a forward berth from her low draw.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Merrimack and Always Perfect fight it out up front and the soft ground drains their finishing effort, the hold-up horses sweep past a spent lead.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set an honest-to-hot gallop that degrades quickly on Good To Soft turf, opening a clear lane for runners who have conserved energy in the final furlong; Sandown's flat 5f offers no hiding place for a stopping leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Always Perfect breaks best and Merrimack is unable to match her early speed, a single front-runner dictates a more regulated gallop that suits her profile.
scenarios.body: A calmer tempo from the front reduces the pace premium and rewards the horse who has dictated, as rivals find less cover to produce their challenge; Always Perfect's recent course and distance form on similar going underpins this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace battle burns itself out before two furlongs and a prominent tracker can find a clean passage to collar the leaders approaching the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Adalida or Hint Of Humour, sitting just off the speed, can exploit any faltering by the front pair and sustain their effort to the line with the benefit of a racing rhythm; the Good To Soft ground does not preclude this but demands they have not expended energy in early traffic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Late
scenarios.trigger: If the entire early group runs to a standstill and a deep hold-up horse produces an unusually strong late surge to pick them all off.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the pace to be truly punishing and for midfield types to find a trouble-free passage through a field that has bunched mid-race — conditions that are plausible but stack several uncertainties; Moe's Legacy with viable soft-ground form is the profile most suited if this extreme shape materialises.

watchPoints.text: Merrimack and Always Perfect will battle head-to-head for the lead from the off — watch whether either shows signs of weakening inside the two-furlong marker, as a capitulation there opens the race to closers.
Lazzar, a natural prominent type, is mapped to midfield due to field congestion — watch for him being crowded on the rail early around the 4-furlong mark where the squeeze is most likely.

Havana Smile is the Scorecard's top selection but carries low confidence and is ridden by a 7lb claimer — watch the market to see whether support arrives, as lack of money would be a meaningful flag against the soft-ground angle.

Isle Of Lismore draws stall 1 with Billy Loughnane aboard — watch whether Loughnane attempts to push forward to a prominent berth early, which could further crowd the prominent group and intensify the pace battle.

Going is logged as Good To Soft throughout the card at Sandown, not the Soft declared in race conditions — any firming in the ground mid-afternoon would marginally favour the front-runners over the hold-up profile this analysis favours.

runners_data.name: Norham
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Sandown last time, trainer Adam Kirby sends out 0/7 over 14 days so no strong handler form, but the horse's prominent style from stall 3 should let Cieren Fallon slot in comfortably behind the early pace duel; the step up to a mile on soft ground looks the key stamina question given a previous outing over just 5f.|
runners_data.comment: Norham bounced back to win last time out, which is an obvious tick, and he has run over today's trip before, but a fourth two starts back tempers expectations slightly, and carrying 130 lb from stall 3 makes this a tough ask at a rating of 79.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Burgundy
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon has 2/52 over 14 days but the yard fires in these types; a confirmed front-runner from stall 5 who will actively contest early supremacy with Cilician, and his form string of 3-1-4 shows a genuine winner under similar conditions — however, getting into a duel from the wider draw against a horse on the rail could drain his reserves.|
runners_data.comment: Duke Of Burgundy won two starts back and shaped with promise when third three starts back, boasting experience over today's trip and going; the main concern is a trainer operating at just 4% in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Drum Bay
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett has been in excellent form (9/47, T14) and this horse's placed form of 2-3 over similar trips and good ground suggests a consistent type who will travel prominently; the stall 4 draw situates Drum Bay ideally between the two pace-setters to take a sit and pounce, and 30 days since last run for a Beckett 2yo usually means they arrive fresh and ready.|
runners_data.comment: Drum Bay arrives here in decent nick after back-to-back placed efforts — second two starts back and third last time out — yet to score in recent starts, and while he has experience over today's trip and conditions, our rating of 76 suggests he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Bent
runners_data.note: Won last time out and the headgear (ht) is retained which is an important positive flag; Jason Watson takes over and Dylan Cunha's 1/24 strike rate over 14 days is modest, but a horse who has hit form wearing that headgear and steps up sharply in trip from 6f to 1m on soft ground is the key question — the ground and distance are both new territory.|
runners_data.comment: Whiskey Bent arrives on the back of a win last time out, has going experience to call on, and his 83 rating underlines his place among the main dangers here; the worry is that he was seventh three starts back, raising a question mark over consistency.

runners_data.name: Clive The Writer
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Sandown on his latest start which is a significant course form positive; De Sousa partners from stall 7 and William Muir & Chris Grassick have 1/16 over 14 days, suggesting modest current handler form, but the horse's midfield style means he needs the pace to be genuinely strong to get involved late over this mile on good-to-soft.|
runners_data.comment: Clive The Writer won last time out but that single bright spot is hard to build a case around, ranked seventh of eight on our figures and carrying 130 lb from stall seven; he has run over today's trip, though the speed rating of 58 does little to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Tiora Time
runners_data.note: Good recent form (3-1-2) with two wins over 6-7f on good ground and the same trip connections, but this horse is a natural prominent racer; the congested pace scenario means it is unlikely to secure its preferred berth just behind the lead, and racing out of its natural position against a genuine front-runner in Cilician from a wider draw dampens its immediate prospects.|
runners_data.comment: Tiora Time arrives here on the back of a win two starts back and a runner-up finish last time out, boasting experience of today's trip and conditions; carrying 128 lb from stall two is the key question mark, but her profile makes her a genuine threat.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 84 and Brian Meehan has 3/11 over 14 days, a strong handler angle; Billy Loughnane takes the ride from stall 1, the optimal draw to control the pace, and while the recent form string shows inconsistency (2-0-2-2-8-4), the ability to dominate from the front on a flat mile on good-to-soft suits his profile — this is the race shape built around him.|
runners_data.comment: Cilician arrives here in fine shape just a fortnight since his last outing, and that second three starts back gives him a clear form platform, bolstered by a rating of 93 that puts him clear of his seven rivals; yet to win in recent starts, but he shapes as the one to beat from stall one off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Crown Ranger
runners_data.note: Marco Botti has 5/17 over 14 days and Marco Ghiani is a reliable pilot, but the form string of 6-5-3 shows consistent placings without winning; this horse is a natural prominent racer who has been mapped to the rear because the field is dense with pace — it is unlikely to enjoy the hold-up role it is shown in, and its chance is tempered by the probability of racing further back than ideal.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Crown Ranger faces a stiff task here; third last time out offers a crumb of comfort, and he has run over today's trip and going before, but 127 lb from stall eight makes life no easier.

races.paceDynamic: Cilician (draw 1) and Duke Of Burgundy (draw 5) are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, creating a genuine two-horse duel from the gates on this flat Sandown mile over good-to-soft ground. That contested pace is unlikely to be truly suicidal but will sustain an honest gallop throughout, compressing the field and leaving little room for closers to manufacture a finishing burst from off the pace. The sustained nature of a two-horse pace argument on soft-leaning ground over a mile favours horses with genuine stamina and the ability to track a strong gallop — prominent racers who can sit just behind the duel and pounce from a position of comfort are the primary beneficiaries here. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Cilician holds draw 1 and is likeliest to control matters from the front, while Tiora Time — a genuine prominent racer — is displaced to midfield in the map and Crown Ranger, also naturally prominent, is shown at the rear, meaning neither will race in their preferred slot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cilician Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician secures the lead from stall 1 and sets a strong but measured tempo that grinds rivals into submission on good-to-soft ground.
scenarios.body: Cilician dictates from draw 1, forcing Duke Of Burgundy to either chase or concede, and the sustained honest gallop on soft-ish ground suits a horse with proven stamina at this trip; the pace setters who fight for control will find this shape reward the one who can sustain rather than sprint.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the Cilician-Duke Of Burgundy duel burns both front-runners off and a prominent sit-just-off-the-pace runner picks up the pieces.
scenarios.body: A genuinely contested lead on good-to-soft at Sandown over a mile often sees the lead-burners tire in the final furlong, leaving the horse who tracked from second or third to sweep through; Drum Bay and Whiskey Bent both carry OK going flags and have the stamina profile to capitalise on front-runners running into the ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stayer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and the front-runners collapse, allowing a genuine stayer tracking from midfield to reel in a strung-out field.
scenarios.body: Clive The Writer drops back to midfield under De Sousa and, if the gallop is honest enough, could produce a sustained late effort on ground that rewards stamina over raw speed; however this shape requires the front-runners to genuinely burn each other out, which is uncertain given Cilician's class edge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Duke Of Burgundy concedes the lead cheaply and Cilician idles, producing a false pace that collapses before the straight.
scenarios.body: A muddled or artificially slow pace would theoretically suit hold-up horses arriving late, but Crown Ranger — the only runner shown at the rear — is a natural prominent type redistributed there, meaning genuine hold-up ability in this field is thin; the scenario is structurally unlikely given two confirmed pace horses in the field.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Cilician from stall 1 immediately takes the lead or whether Duke Of Burgundy from stall 5 pushes across — if Cilician is forced to race wide or hunt the pace early, his hold on the shape weakens materially.

Drum Bay's trainer Ralph Beckett is in sharp 14-day form (9/47) and the horse's stall 4 position places it perfectly to track a duel — if Beckett's horses are running well at the meeting, upgrade Drum Bay's threat.

Whiskey Bent retained the headgear that coincided with its last-time-out win; if it jumps well and slots behind the pace, the headgear factor on a horse stepping up sharply in trip could make it a live each-way threat despite the distance question.

Tiora Time and Crown Ranger are both natural prominent types racing out of position in this map — if either manages to secure a berth closer to the pace than the model shows, they become considerably more dangerous than their mapped role suggests.

Going is reported as Good-to-Soft across all Sandown races today despite the race conditions listing Soft — treat the ground as on the easier side of GTS rather than genuinely soft, which slightly reduces the stamina premium and keeps speed-oriented runners relevant.

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent form cluster (4th-5th range) at 7f on Good ground suggests consistent but not winning level; Richard Hannon yard not firing sharply (T14:2/52) which is a concern, and the horse's seven-run sequence without a win at 7f on similar going tempers expectations despite the profile suiting the pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back and fourth on his most recent outing, Christian David arrives on decent fitness at 27 days, with experience over today's trip and going and a rating of 90 to underpin his claims — though a winless recent run of six and a trainer operating at just 4% are real concerns.

runners_data.name: Huscal
runners_data.note: Recent form is progressive with a win and place in last two starts including a 7f Sandown victory on Standard going; Charles Hills yard in solid form (4/20 T14) and Marco Ghiani retains the ride; hold-up style suits this pace shape and soft-going is flagged as acceptable.
runners_data.comment: Huscal arrives in excellent nick, winning last time out and placing in two of his three most recent starts, and he has experience of both today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall one carrying 131 lb is the factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Carries top weight (135lbs) and his soft-going record is poor — finishing 11th and 14th in his two runs on soft — which significantly undermines his chance despite the highest OR in the field; midfield style means he needs the pace to collapse, which is unlikely with a controlled front-runner, and Billy Loughnane will need a perfect trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, The Angel King nonetheless finished second two starts back and shaped with more promise than his overall record suggests; he has experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 93 gives him an edge over his rivals, though the trainer's lean spell is worth a note.

runners_data.name: Zabeel Alkabeir
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the race and will dictate the fractions from stall 5, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) and the note that he is racing out of role should moderate expectations of him winning; 71 days off and his sole soft-going run produced an 11th, so his ability to last home on this ground after making all is the key question.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and returning from a 71-day break, Zabeel Alkabeir is hard to fancy despite two wins in his last four starts; he has experience of today's distance and going, but a speed rating of 75 leaves him with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: Midfield runner with a strong record at 7f on Good and Standard going, including a win and multiple places in recent history; blinkers noted (hg:p) and Cieren Fallon takes over in a yard running at 4/17 in the 14-day window, suggesting the stable is in form.
runners_data.comment: Philanthropist shaped with real promise when runner-up last time out, and having already shown experience over today's trip and conditions, he arrives here fit on a 30-day break carrying 130 lb; the risk is that his two starts back yielded an unplaced effort that questions his consistency.

runners_data.name: Sea Founder
runners_data.note: Prominent racer drawn ideally in stall 2 to track the lone front-runner throughout; has won at 7f on Standard and placed at 7f on the same track, though soft-ground form (9th over 10f on Soft) is less convincing; Jason Watson will look to exploit the rail position.

races.paceDynamic: Zabeel Alkabeir is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 7f handicap on Good to Soft ground at Sandown, with Sea Founder likely to press or track closely from draw 2 as the other prominent-style runner. With only one true pace-setter and no rival willing to contest for the lead, Zabeel Alkabeir should control fractions comfortably, setting a measured and sustainable gallop that keeps the race relatively compressed until the home straight. The soft-ish ground will ensure the pace is honest enough without becoming a true test, meaning the early positions will be genuinely advantageous. This shape favours hold-up and midfield horses who can travel within striking distance and produce a sustained finish from two furlongs out — notably those with proven form at 7f on testing ground — rather than closers needing a collapse in front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Zabeel Alkabeir dictates a steady, uncontested gallop and the field settles in compact shape into the straight.
scenarios.body: Zabeel Alkabeir controls fractions without pressure, keeping the pace honest but not punishing, allowing hold-up horses with strong finishes to reel in the front-runner across the soft ground in the final two furlongs. Huscal and Philanthropist, both holding midfield or hold-up profiles with recent competitive form, are ideally placed to exploit this shape with their sustained finishes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Founder tracks Zabeel Alkabeir closely and the pace proves moderate enough to reward positional racing.
scenarios.body: Sea Founder, drawn 2 and comfortable racing prominently, can sit directly behind the leader and get a dream tow into the straight, using that prime position to outstay rivals on ground that rewards those who conserve energy early. With a win and a place on Flat-type courses at 7f, Sea Founder has the profile to hold on if the pace is genuinely slow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Soft deteriorates or the early pace is quicker than expected, turning this into a genuine stamina examination.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-anticipated gallop combined with the testing surface would drain the field and hand a premium to those with the deepest reserves, with The Angel King's softer-ground second (2/7f/GOO adjacent form) and Philanthropist's proven staying power at 7f potentially coming into play. However, The Angel King's poor recent soft-going record (11th and 14th) caps confidence in this shape delivering for him.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Denied, Pace Too Slow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so sedate that hold-up horses cannot get competitive runs and prominent types steal an unassailable advantage.
scenarios.body: An extremely slow gallop means hold-up horses like Christian David and Huscal find themselves with too much ground to make up in the final furlong, and the race is effectively over by the two-furlong pole for those tracking from off the pace. This is the least likely shape given Zabeel Alkabeir's natural front-running style, which tends to produce a decent clip.

watchPoints.text: Huscal's draw in stall 1 means Marco Ghiani must decide early whether to push forward or tuck in; if he fails to get a clean run on the rail turning in, his hold-up finish could be compromised in a six-runner field.

Zabeel Alkabeir has been off 71 days and his only soft-ground start yielded an 11th — if he tires sharply in the final furlong after setting the fractions, the race could open up chaotically for whichever prominent horse is tracking him.

The Angel King's top weight of 135lbs in soft conditions is a significant burden; watch for Billy Loughnane attempting to conserve energy early, as any cover lost on the wide draw (stall 6) could cost him dearly.

Sea Founder's proximity to the pace from stall 2 makes her a live danger if the gallop is genuinely slow; Jason Watson will be under no pressure to cover up and could steal a march on the hold-up horses if the tempo drops mid-race.

Richard Hannon's yard is notably cold at 2/52 over 14 days — Christian David's chance may hinge on the horse's own ability to find form despite the trainer's current flat patch, making the first two furlongs important to assess whether he travels fluently.

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea

runners_data.comment: Lyra Lea brings strong recent form to the table, finishing third last time out and a winner three starts back, and she has experience of both today's trip and conditions with a quick eight-day turnaround suggesting she is in peak condition. The main risk is that she faces stiffer company on her current official mark.

runners_data.name: Gesayed
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's 3yo has form on good ground and arrives fresh off an 83-day break; drawn ideally in stall 1 and confirmed as the sole front-runner, she controls pace but her recent best form is on better ground and the soft going is a minor reservation.|
runners_data.comment: Gesayed showed she could win when scoring four starts back, and a third three starts back underlines her ability, but the 83-day break is the concern despite a trainer firing at 31% recently.

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Decent recent placed form but soft-ground numbers are thin with only one similar-going run in her last eight; a natural pace-presser whose role in this race will likely be compromised — she is unlikely to get her favoured prominent berth and the STYLE_FIT figure (0.94) tempers her prospects accordingly.|
runners_data.comment: Brisk Symphony arrives here on the back of a placing in her last five starts and is fit on just sixteen days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and conditions working in her favour; the concern is that she has been winless in recent starts and must prove she can convert.

runners_data.name: Vanilla Skies
runners_data.note: William Haggas's lightly-raced sort has strong form figures — three runs, 1-2-2 — and clearly has ability; she runs in headgear and wants to race prominently, but with multiple rivals ahead of her in the queue for that position, her chance is capped by not getting her natural role.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Vanilla Skies is hard to fancy at a nine-pound deficit to her official rating, though she has placed in two of her last three starts, was a winner three starts back, and has run over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Dream Vega
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's 3yo last won over this course-and-distance on good, has finished 1-2-4 in her three career starts, and at OR 78 represents a consistent performer; races prominently and should be able to take up a position close to Gesayed, making her a strong fit for the dominant scenario.|
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and second two starts back give Dream Vega a decent recent profile, but ranked seventh of eight on our figures she faces a stiff ask, and 62 days off the track adds an element of doubt.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard top selection carries genuine form — 123121 is a striking sequence — and Andrew Balding's yard are firing with 13 wins from 69 in 14 days; a natural prominent racer who is likely to find herself further back than ideal in this shape, so the redistribution caveat (STYLE_FIT 0.92) should temper win confidence even as the scorecard flags her as the headline selection.|
runners_data.comment: Allegrino arrives in fine fettle after a win last time out, and her recent sequence of three wins in her last six starts underlines consistent form, though a mark of 76 and 130 lb from stall 8 add pressure on a filly who has run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Distant Shore
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's highest-rated runner in the field (OR 82) has placed twice at 8f on good but has drifted back in trip here; wears headgear and is a confirmed hold-up type — Jack Mitchell will need the pace to be stronger than a lone front-runner typically generates, which structurally limits her scenario.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent filly who has finished second twice in her last five starts, and her experience over today's trip and conditions bolsters her claims; she carries 136 lb from stall 3, and though winless in recent starts, an 88 rating atop this field makes her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Souffler
runners_data.note: Won over this course and trip on good ground, has a clear course affinity, and Kevin Philippart De Foy's yard is in form; a prominent runner who may be better placed than some rivals to slot just behind the pace, though recent form (6-1-6) is stop-start and the soft ground is a slight unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Souffler won one start back but has been sixth in two of her four most recent outings, and while she has run over today's trip and going before, her rating of 78 and 133 lb burden make a return to that winning form far from assured.

races.paceDynamic: Gesayed breaks from stall 1 as the sole confirmed front-runner and should stride into an uncontested lead through the early stages of this 7f Sandown contest on soft ground, setting a sustainable gallop rather than a pressured one. The field holds more prominent-type runners than the race shape can accommodate — Brisk Symphony, Vanilla Skies, and Allegrino are all natural pace-presser types who will find themselves shuffled into midfield as Gesayed dictates terms unchallenged. Dream Vega and Lyra Lea are the prominent runners most likely to actually secure a forward position and sit closest to the pace, with Souffler potentially tracking just behind. With Gesayed controlling fractions on soft ground at Sandown's flat, sweeping track, this shape decisively favours horses who can sit in a close-up position and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs — a premium on prominent racers with proven soft-ground finishing ability rather than hold-up horses who will face a wall of traffic or genuine closers who must work too hard from the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gesayed Controls, Closest Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gesayed dictates a steady-to-moderate gallop unchallenged and the race is run to suit those sitting just behind the pace.
scenarios.body: Gesayed sets the tempo from stall 1 and the race develops into a test of staying power on soft ground, rewarding those who have travelled smoothly in second or third; the horse that has tracked the pace with least fuss and has the best finishing reserves claims the spoils close home.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Gesayed Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop Gesayed sets is genuinely modest and no rival lands a telling blow until too late.
scenarios.body: Soft ground has historically suited front-runners at Sandown when the pace is measured and rivals leave their challenge too late; Gesayed's recent form, though patchy, shows she can dictate and she is drawn ideally in stall 1 with Billy Loughnane aboard.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Presser Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the race fractures early and one of the naturally prominent types manages to secure a better position than the pace map suggests.
scenarios.body: Should early jostling create gaps, Allegrino or Vanilla Skies — both capable of travelling prominently when space allows — could find themselves better placed than their mapped position implies, but their STYLE_FIT discounts make this a lower-probability shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to set up a strong late run from the back.
scenarios.body: Distant Shore has the highest OR in the field and holds proven placed form at this trip, but her hold-up style on soft ground at Sandown requires the tempo to be significantly stronger than a lone front-runner typically generates; this shape is structurally the least likely given a single unchallenged pace-setter.

watchPoints.text: Gesayed (stall 1) jumps cleanly and is unchallenged — if she controls the first three furlongs without any of the prominent pack pressing her, the race shape locks in around the pace-tracking scenario immediately.|

Brisk Symphony, Vanilla Skies, and Allegrino are all prominent types who cannot all secure their natural position — watch the first furlong for traffic and shuffling that could compromise two or all three of them from the outset.|

Allegrino is the Strand Scorecard top pick but is mapped to midfield due to redistribution — if she fails to assert early and finds herself trapped in a pocket on the rail, her chance diminishes significantly despite her strong form figures.|

Distant Shore arrives as the highest-rated runner but is a hold-up type relying on a strong gallop that a single front-runner on soft is unlikely to supply — if the pace is modest through the first half, her finishing effort may simply arrive in the wrong place.|

The going is officially recorded as Good To Soft across the card despite the race being carded as Soft — worth monitoring any update near post time, as a firmer surface would alter the stamina premium and potentially favour quicker-actioned types like Vanilla Skies.|

races.name: Sporting Times Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Tipsy Tiger
runners_data.note: A proven hold-up performer with strong form in similar going (3 from 4 in soft/yielding conditions), returning from 74 days off which is worth monitoring, but the distance and conditions suit; Laura Coughlan takes the ride and the horse wears a hood, suggesting some freshness to manage.
runners_data.comment: Tipsy Tiger shaped with promise when third three starts back and fourth two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going to call on; the main risk is a 74-day absence leaving him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: Trained by Ralph Beckett who has been in strong form (9/47 over 14 days), this 3yo has good recent form at 10f on good ground and steps up marginally in conditions — the soft surface is untested but the trip looks right and recency is a plus at just 14 days since last run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though a second three starts back and a third four starts back hint at ability, and she returns on a quick 14-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going; 131 lb from stall seven is the limiting factor.

runners_data.name: Plan C
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners, Plan C has been off the track 91 days — the fitness question is real — and while it won over soft ground previously (1 win from 3 in sim-going), setting a strong pace after a break on a testing surface is a significant ask; Alan King's form figures are modest at 1/14.

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: The most in-form of the front-runners with three wins in recent starts, Del Corso is lightly weighted at OR=72 and has Ed Walker's backing (6/45 recent strike rate); however, this horse's sim-going record shows no wins or places in soft conditions, which is a concern when the stamina race develops.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Del Corso is hard to fancy despite a placed effort last time out; he does have experience of today's distance and going, and 27 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but the speed rating of 66 makes him difficult to support with confidence.

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3yo holds genuine hold-up tendencies but is pushed toward midfield by the numbers — wearing a visor for the first time, the headgear change is notable; the STYLE_FIT tag means its chance is conditional on getting closer to the pace than it naturally would, and soft-going form is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mr Seagull nevertheless shaped with promise when fourth last time out and arrives here 26 days later in solid order; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 84 makes him a confident pick on overall profile.

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: The highest-rated runner in the race at OR=80 and a winner over this exact 1m2f trip in good-to-soft, Royal Poetry is the natural pace-setter and Richard Hannon's team send him here with strong course-form credentials; the risk is he has to do too much work in a three-runner pace battle.
runners_data.comment: Royal Poetry landed a winning blow three starts back and has since shown consistent form, with a second two starts back keeping her in the mix; she has experience of today's distance and going, though the trainer's lean spell — just 2/47 in the last 14 days — is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Dancing Tiger
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's 4yo is a genuine hold-up horse — the map places it in midfield but its natural inclination is to race from the rear — with a strong soft-ground profile (1 win and 3 places from 8 sim-going runs) and a recent run 11 days ago suggesting it is fit and ready; the STRAND top pick with medium confidence, and the soft conditions over 1m2f genuinely play to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Tiger showed well when second three starts back, and again four starts back, but has failed to build on that in recent outings, finishing unplaced last time; experience over today's trip and going helps, though 137 lb is a stern test from stall two.

runners_data.name: Letmebetheboss
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 5yo won over 14f on soft ground and ran well in similar conditions, so the stamina profile is genuine; at OR=65 it is the lowest-rated runner in the field but its soft-going record (1W1P from 4) is legitimate and apprentice jockey Myla Coppins claims 5lb — the weight advantage could be relevant if the leaders capitulate.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and drawn in stall eight, Letmebetheboss has struggled for consistency in recent starts — seventh last time out and fourth two back — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win four starts back shows he can find the line first.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a contested, strong gallop from the off over this 1m2f trip on Good To Soft ground — stamina will be the decisive currency, not tactical speed. The three leaders will fight for position early, driving up the pace to a level that will stretch the field and expose any lack of resolution in the straight. This shape strongly favours horses with proven stamina who can be delivered late and pick up a weakening lead, making genuine hold-up and midfield types the primary beneficiaries — provided they can get their natural position. The field holds more genuine rear-of-field types than can all sit where they want: Dancing Tiger and Mr Seagull are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and Royal Poetry — as the highest-rated of the three leaders and experienced over this exact trip — is most likely to actually control the front, with Plan C and Del Corso likely to press but potentially over-extend themselves.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stayers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso burn each other out setting a strong pace, leaving the race wide open for a stamina-laden finisher.
scenarios.body: The three leaders trade blows on a soft surface over 1m2f and empty in the final two furlongs, handing the race to a horse who has been travelling within itself; soft-ground stamina becomes the defining quality and runners who have demonstrated resolution in similar conditions thrive.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstays Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Poetry dictates a controlled but honest gallop and proves the classiest stayer in the field, the leaders do not destroy each other and the best horse simply stays on strongest.
scenarios.body: Royal Poetry's proven ability over 1m2f and his Soft-ground experience allows him to control fractions enough to preserve his stamina, never fully capitulating under pressure; the challengers find him too durable and he holds on as the held-up horses arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly ferocious and collapses sharply, a horse with a dash of finishing speed from midfield gets the run of the race and cuts through beaten rivals.
scenarios.body: Molo Del Palazzo, trained by Ralph Beckett and returning from a recent run, can be delivered from a central position into a gap; if the leaders genuinely tie each other up, a clean passage could reward a horse with scope for improvement at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Threat Materialises
scenarios.trigger: If traffic allows Dancing Tiger or Mr Seagull to get closer to the pace than their redistribution suggests, negating the positional disadvantage.
scenarios.body: Both horses are genuine hold-up types whose natural position is further back than the crowded rear of this field permits, meaning any clear run depends on circumstances rather than design; the discounted STYLE_FIT score reflects that this outcome requires things to go right against the grain of the race shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Plan C, returning from 91 days off, sets out to lead aggressively — if it goes for the front hard, it risks burning itself out and dragging Royal Poetry and Del Corso into an unsustainably fierce gallop that ruins all three leaders.

Del Corso has no wins or places on soft ground in its history — if conditions are genuinely testing, its recent winning form on good ground may not translate and it could be a false pace-setter who fades when the race gets serious.

Dancing Tiger and Mr Seagull are both true hold-up types packed into a midfield cluster — watch for traffic congestion in the straight if the field concertinas as the pace collapses, which could deny either a clear run.

Royal Poetry has the highest OR (80) and proven 1m2f soft-ground form, but as the natural leader it must do its own work in a strongly-contested pace — if it has to fight for the lead early, its stamina may be compromised by the final furlong.

Letmebetheboss carries the lowest weight (127lbs) with a 5lb claimer — if the pace is truly relentless and the leaders empty, its soft-ground stamina over staying trips could make it a bigger player than its OR=65 suggests.
